answers.question: Here is the smallest tool set in which every write has one call and every fact the agent needs before it acts has a read. Please confirm it. (1) List the signed-in customer's orders: returns each order with its number, placed date, status, line items, shipping cost, tax, total paid, payment method, and its refund or none; the call can get no answer. (2) Cancel an order, by order number: answers "cancelled", answers "not cancellable" when the order has shipped since the agent read it, or gets no answer. (3) Issue the refund for an order, by order number: answers with the refund, issued, and the amount refunded; or a refund with status failed on a terminal error; or a transient error that creates no refund; or gets no answer. (4) Create a staff follow-up task, with the order number and one reason: refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown, and a fourth reason, refund amount differs, for a refund that came back with another amount than the customer said yes to; the call answers "created" or gets no answer. Claims put to the owner: C-05, C-06, C-09, C-16, C-17.
answers.recommended: Yes, that is the tool set, with those answers and the fourth reason added.
answers.reply:
> Q3 Proposed fields. Order: order number (e.g. HG-10482), placed date, status, line items (product name, quantity, unit price), shipping cost, tax, total paid, payment method (e.g. "Visa ending 4242"). Refund: refund id (e.g. RF-5531), order number, amount, payment method, status (pending, issued). No final-sale flag.
> - Refund status: pending, issued, failed.
> - Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common order systems. In those, a cancel call that gets no answer may still have cancelled the order, and reading an order right after a refund call shows the refund that call made. If that holds here, the agent never sends a second cancel call after one that got no answer, and after a refund call with no answer it trusts the order read again to say whether the refund was issued. If it does not hold, an unanswered cancel call could be sent again safely, and the read after an unanswered refund call could not settle the refund. Is that how your system behaves? Claims put to the owner: C-07, C-11.
answers.recommended: Yes: a cancel call with no answer may have cancelled the order, and the order list shows a refund as soon as it is made.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> - Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.
> Q3 Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off. For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.

answers.question: When the cancel call gets no answer, the agent cannot tell whether the order was cancelled. The shortest path: the customer asks to cancel the order by its number; the agent lists the orders; it proposes cancelling the order and refunding its total; the customer says yes; the agent sends the cancel call; the call gets no answer. What should the agent do next?
answers.recommended: Send no second cancel call and no refund call, create a staff task with the reason cancellation unknown, and tell the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled, no refund was sent, and staff will follow up.
answers.reply:
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
> - One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.

answers.question: When the staff follow-up call gets no answer, the agent does not send it again, so it cannot tell whether staff has the case. The shortest path: the customer says yes; the cancel call answers "cancelled"; the refund call answers failed; the agent creates a staff task; the call gets no answer. What does the agent tell the customer?
answers.recommended: It tells the customer what happened to the order and the refund, says it could not confirm the case reached staff, and asks them to contact the store.
answers.reply:
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 2. Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process. One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
